subject: History
description: Covers Fa-Hien, Samudragupta, Nalanda, Iron Pillar.

questions.stem: During the reign of which Gupta emperor did the famous Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa-Hien (Faxian) visit India?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Fa-Hien was the first major Chinese pilgrim to visit India. He traveled overland via the Silk Road and arrived in India around 399 CE during the reign of Chandragupta II (also known as Vikramaditya), the zenith of the Gupta Empire. He came to acquire authentic Buddhist texts and heavily praised the peaceful and prosperous administration of the Guptas.
DECOY BUSTING: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) is the other extremely famous Chinese pilgrim, but he visited much later in the 7th century during the reign of King Harsha (Harshavardhana), not the Guptas.
EXAM INSIGHT: Interestingly, in Fa-Hien's extensive travelogue 'Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms', he meticulously details the social and religious conditions of India but completely fails to mention the emperor's name (Chandragupta II) even once.

questions.stem: Which great ruler of the Gupta dynasty is often referred to as the 'Napoleon of India' due to his extensive and aggressive military conquests?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Samudragupta was the second emperor of the Gupta Dynasty. He was a brilliant military tactician who vastly expanded the empire's borders. The British historian V.A. Smith famously dubbed him the "Napoleon of India" because of his unbroken string of military victories across the Indian subcontinent, from the Himalayas to Kanchipuram.
DECOY BUSTING: Chandragupta Maurya belongs to a completely different, older dynasty. Chandragupta I was Samudragupta's father. Skandagupta is famous for repelling the devastating Huna (Hun) invasions.
EXAM INSIGHT: Samudragupta's conquests are detailed in the famous Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti), composed in brilliant Sanskrit by his court poet Harishena.

questions.stem: Who founded the ancient Nalanda University, one of the greatest centers of learning in the ancient world?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Nalanda University, located in modern-day Bihar, was established during the 5th century CE by the Gupta emperor Kumargupta I (who assumed the title Shakraditya). It grew to become a massive residential university attracting thousands of students from China, Korea, Japan, and Tibet to study Mahayana Buddhism, logic, grammar, and medicine.
DECOY BUSTING: Dharmapala (of the Pala dynasty) founded the equally famous Vikramashila University. Ashoka lived centuries earlier.
EXAM INSIGHT: Nalanda was brutally destroyed and its massive library burnt to the ground in 1193 CE by the invading Turkish general Bakhtiyar Khilji.

questions.stem: The iconic Iron Pillar located in the Qutb Minar complex in Delhi, famous for its incredible resistance to rust over 1600 years, was erected in honor of which king?

options.option_text: King Chandra (widely identified as Chandragupta II)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Iron Pillar of Delhi bears a Sanskrit inscription stating it was erected as a standard in honor of Lord Vishnu by a king named "Chandra". Historians universally identify this king as Chandragupta II of the Gupta Dynasty. The pillar is a testament to the highly advanced metallurgical skills of ancient Indians, as it has not rusted despite centuries of exposure to the elements.
DECOY BUSTING: Ashoka erected stone pillars, not iron ones. Qutb-ud-din Aibak built the surrounding mosque and minar much later. Prithviraj Chauhan ruled Delhi just before the Turkish conquest.
EXAM INSIGHT: The pillar was originally located in Udayagiri (Madhya Pradesh) and was moved to its current location in Delhi much later, likely by the Tomar Rajputs in the 11th century.
